proposal.implementation_plan: Edit target as primary plus train. In build_target, keep the native long_view label as the returned main target exactly as now, but also compute an auxiliary train-only regression target from DV.watch_ratio(): use valid mask and transformed ratio r = log1p(clip(ratio,0,None))/12. Store this auxiliary array in a module-level structure keyed by train rows. In train, replace delegated SO.train with a local two-stage implementation that exactly reproduces the visible LightGBM LambdaRank fixed parameters/grouping for the main objective, then fits a second LightGBM regressor on the same feature matrix and train rows for the auxiliary watch-ratio target using only rows with valid watch_ratio. research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

review.analysis: Not a duplicate. The only overlapping memory (m009) was an implementation/runtime failure on a different operator stack (deepfm_engagement_mtl_v1) with a shared neural auxiliary head and unproven prediction-path integration. This proposal targets item_lambdarank and makes the auxiliary branch contribute through an explicit local two-model LightGBM training and fixed score fusion in predict, so the prior failure does not falsify the mechanism itself. It also preserves long_view as the primary ranking label rather than replacing it, consistent with the contract and distinct from the negative soft-label experiment m010.
review.novelty_or_new_evidence: Material implementation difference: instead of a shared-head custom DeepFM with opaque delegated predict behavior, this proposal uses a visible second LightGBM regressor on train-only DV.watch_ratio() with explicit nonzero blending into the main LambdaRank score at inference. New evidence remains source-backed by E003 and additionally aligns with the diagnostic that aux_weight is currently inert unless implemented visibly.

rejected: A fixed monotone compression of LambdaRank scores will slightly improve nDCG@5 and portfolio marginality by reducing overconfident top-item separation without changing the underlying feature model.

A small train-only watch-ratio auxiliary branch, combined with the native long_view LambdaRank score, will improve top-k ordering by separating items with similar long_view propensity but different likely watch depth, yielding either standalone lift or portfolio-diverse gains.
selection_rationale:
Candidate 0 is connected and cheap, but it is a predict-only monotone transform on an intra-user ranking task where monotone reshaping usually leaves ordering nearly unchanged; its own evidence base includes two recent predict-edit negatives on the same parent path (m005, m006). Those are not an exact mechanism match, so the candidate is not formally ineligible, but they materially reduce reliability for a small, speculative gain. In a stagnation-escape portfolio setting, a credible tiny refinement with weak standalone effect and likely high rank-correlation to the parent is less attractive than a structurally different error source.

Candidate 1 best matches the directive. It is a connected executable change in the features consumer, not an inert config tweak. It directly addresses a concrete diagnostic/code gap: current delegated features are described as 25 fixed context/group-stat columns, while the task requires personalization through user-candidate interactions. Train-only user-author/user-video/user-tab affinity counts are legal at inference because they are aggregates keyed only by IDs available then, and they should alter ranking within user rather than just add per-user constants. It is also explicitly an error-diversifier, which is valuable under an active portfolio and stagnation. The popularity-slice losses, especially on rarer items, provide a plausible dataset-specific reason these memorization-style affinities could help marginal portfolio gain. Implementation risk is moderate but manageable, with no need to reimplement training logic.

Candidate 2 has the strongest mechanism novelty and some curated research support, but the evidence is adapted from a different architecture/objective setup and therefore weaker than direct dataset/code diagnostics. More importantly, it requires replacing delegated training with a local two-model LightGBM pipeline while faithfully reproducing grouping and fixed parameters. That creates substantial implementation and attribution risk: a negative or positive result would be harder to trust as due to the auxiliary-target hypothesis alone rather than training reimplementation differences. In a one-change-at-a-time regime prioritizing evidential and implementation reliability, this is too brittle for the next measured experiment despite potentially larger upside.

Therefore Candidate 1 has the highest expected valid-primary marginal portfolio gain after reliability adjustment, with better portfolio diversification than Candidate 0 and much lower implementation risk than Candidate 2.
